SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Newspapers/Magazines Twisters, part of MONEY Suggested vocabulary: tax, pay, business, collect, money, honest, profit,  in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to read newspapers and magazines? 2. How do we choose the materials we read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Newspapers/Magazines Twisters in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Newspapers/Magazines Twisters in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the importance of prepositions for clarity in communication. • Learners are guided to identify prepositions in samples of oral or written text sentences. • Learners are guided to play appropriate preposition games online or offline using digital devices with assistive technology. • Learners are guided to construct sentence prepositions. • Learners are guided to complete gaps in sentences, matching prepositions with pictures or picture descriptions. • Learners are guided to complete substitution exercises on various prepositions. • Learners with low vision are guided to watch while learners with blindness listen to audio visual videos clip, visit web pages and other online resources and pick out prepositions. • Learners are guided to use prepositions in a role play or simulation of people paying tax. 1.
